# Uniform affine-buffered depth continuity on positive fiber limits

This note proves the continuity needed to minimize the covariance-
normalized buffered functional on a fixed canonical base. It also
identifies the exact use of ORIGINAL bad-minor minimality in excluding
vanishing fibers. No normalized-buffer restriction inequality is used.

Throughout P is a fixed finite base, d>=1, and all sampled fibers are
positive convex bodies. Compatibility is retained whenever an actual
mixed-body conclusion is stated. Write N=d+1.

## 1. Positive-fiber Hausdorff limits

Suppose K_z^(m)->K_z in Hausdorff distance for every z in P, with every
limit K_z full-dimensional. All bodies lie in one fixed continuous
ball after discarding finitely many indices. Their fiber indicators
converge in L1. Set

    delta_m=max_z d_H(K_z^(m),K_z),
    VDelta_m=sum_z |K_z^(m) symmetric-difference K_z|.

Then delta_m,VDelta_m->0. Fiber masses, first and second moments,
centroids, total mass M_m, and within-fiber covariance Sigma_m all
converge to their corresponding limit quantities. The limiting Sigma
is positive definite. Hence its induced covector norms converge
uniformly on the Euclidean unit sphere:

    eta_m=sup_(|u|=1)|sqrt(u^T Sigma_m u)-sqrt(u^T Sigma u)| ->0.   (1)

This assertion uses the within-fiber covariance, not the covariance of
the discrete base or of the entire physical union.

Let f_m(p,y)=(E_(K_p^(m))(y)/M_m)^(1/N), with the analogous f_0.
Marked energy is jointly continuous under positive-body Hausdorff
convergence, including marks tending to the body boundary. Interior
continuity follows from the attained positive-denominator minimizer;
boundary continuity follows from E<=N T and the marked continuity of
T. It follows by a compactness contradiction that

    omega_m=sup {|f_m(p,y_m)-f_0(p,y)|:
       p in P, y_m in K_p^(m), y in K_p, |y_m-y|<=delta_m} ->0.    (2)

Every point of either body has a corresponding point in the other
with that distance, by the definition of Hausdorff distance. If a
supremum in (2) did not tend to zero, a fixed-base subsequence and a
convergent mark subsequence would contradict marked continuity.

## 2. A uniform cap comparison independent of the base tilt

Use EUCLIDEAN |u|=1 when comparing the two invariant buffered depths.
This is permitted by homogeneity: the threshold in the m-th family is

    a.p+u.y_m-epsilon f_m(p,y_m) Gamma_m(u),
    Gamma_m(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma_m u).

The base tilt a is arbitrary and need not be bounded. Corresponding
sources have the SAME base p, so the a.p term cancels exactly. Put

    Gmax=sup_m sup_(|u|=1) Gamma_m(u),
    Fmax=sup_(p,y in K_p) f_0(p,y) <=1.

For marks in (2), the two thresholds differ by at most

    Delta_m=delta_m+epsilon[Gmax omega_m+Fmax eta_m].              (3)

Choose a uniform bound L on the sum of maximal unit-normal sections
of the original fibers (or of all nearby fibers). For d=1 the bound
is |P|. Comparing the measures first at one fixed threshold costs at
most VDelta_m; moving that threshold by Delta_m costs at most LDelta_m.
Thus for EVERY a and EVERY Euclidean unit u,

    |buffered-cap-mass_m-buffered-cap-mass_0|
                       <=VDelta_m+LDelta_m.                      (4)

There is no term involving ||a||. Proper, saturated, and supporting
closed cuts are all included by the coarea strip bound. At pure-base
cuts only the fiber weights vary, and their mass difference is at
most VDelta_m. Taking the infimum over the same entire family of
directions therefore gives

    |b_(epsilon,m)(p,y_m)-b_(epsilon,0)(p,y)|
                       <=VDelta_m+LDelta_m.                      (5)

This proves UNIFORM convergence along the Hausdorff correspondences,
not merely upper semicontinuity. It remains valid when the parameters
epsilon_m converge to a fixed epsilon: add the uniformly vanishing
term |epsilon_m-epsilon|Gmax sup f_m to (3).

Taking actual maximizing points and their corresponding points in
the other family, in both directions, proves

    Q_epsilon(K^(m))->Q_epsilon(K),
    Q_epsilon(K^(m))/M_m -> Q_epsilon(K)/M.                       (6)

All lattice labels and all oblique caps have been retained. The result
requires positive limiting fibers; it does not silently extend the
normalized energy/covariance construction through zero total mass or
degenerate fibers.

## 3. What original bad-minor minimality supplies

Suppose a canonical base P has been selected by the already established
ORIGINAL-depth attained-minor argument: it is cardinality-minimal among
bad canonical closed minors, with target tau(P), and proper closed
minors T obey tau(T)>=tau(P). Fix a strict number beta_bar<tau(P).

For any family satisfying normalized buffered depth <=beta_bar,
ordinary normalized depth is also <=beta_bar because b_0<=b_epsilon.
Normalize its total mass to one. If a sequence of such families lost
some positive fibers, pass to the positive limiting-mass support T.
Actual anchored inclusions make T closed. Its retained mass tends to
one. The ORIGINAL depth restriction inequality and canonical lift give

    b_original(canonical T)
       <=liminf(original retained-family depths) <=beta_bar
       <tau(P)<=tau(T).

This contradicts original bad-minor minimality. The argument is purely
about original depth and mass restriction. No claim that the normalized
buffered functional is monotone under deleting fibers is required.

In fact this proves a uniform positive mass lower bound on the whole
ordinary-depth sublevel class beta_0<=beta_bar, not just on a particular
buffered minimizing sequence. Otherwise a sequence violating that
bound would give the same smaller original bad minor.

The archived canonical normalization theorem then applies: after common
continuous GL maps and affine fiber shears, the entire sublevel class
has positive fiber-volume lower bounds, common continuous outer-radius
bounds, and positive Hausdorff limits. These coordinate changes preserve
the invariant buffered functional. Equation (6) is therefore the new
continuity input needed for its attained minimum on that class.

This paragraph invokes, rather than reproves, the dependence-connected
canonical normalization and minor machinery in
`candidate c280bb0dcfd30f3d` and its lattice-
completeness correction. The numerical finite-base target of that
archive is false without the required arithmetic hypotheses; no such
unrestricted target is asserted here.

## 4. A uniform small-buffer choice before minimization

The own-properness condition can also be made uniform BEFORE choosing
a buffered minimizer. Work in a normalized compact representative
class from Section 3 with M=1, let m=|P|, and fix uniform constants

    L >= sum maximal unit-normal fiber section areas,
    G >= sqrt(lambda_max(Sigma)).

The ordinary maximal raw depth is at least gamma_d/m, by the centroid
of a largest fiber. Since f=(E/M)^(1/N)<=1, every buffered maximizing
point w satisfies

    b_0(w) >= gamma_d/m-epsilon L G.                             (7)

Original depth is L-Lipschitz within a fixed fiber, uniformly over
arbitrary base tilts. It vanishes on the own-fiber boundary by the
canonical support-majorant argument. Consequently

    dist(w_cont,boundary K_p) >= b_0(w)/L.                        (8)

Choose epsilon so that

    epsilon G < gamma_d/(4mL).                                  (9)

Then (7) is at least 3gamma_d/(4m), whereas the physical continuous
buffer displacement in any Euclidean unit direction is at most
epsilon G<gamma_d/(4mL). Thus every buffered maximizing source has
a uniformly proper own shifted cut, with a strict margin independent
of the family in this sublevel class.

To organize the quantifiers, first choose beta_bar strictly between
the original depth of a given bad family and tau(P). Obtain the compact
sublevel constants from ORIGINAL bad-minor minimality, independently
of epsilon. Then choose epsilon positive small enough for (9) and for
the given family's buffered depth to remain below beta_bar. Minimize
the invariant buffered functional. The resulting minimizing sequence
stays in the original sublevel class and all of the preceding bounds
apply. There is no circular choice of epsilon after the minimizer.

The resulting attainment/regular-own-section interface does not prove
regularity of the OTHER fiber traces, and does not prove the signed
contact response pays the required target.
